doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Versatility: polkas to Isaac Hayes
summary: Answering the phone for any gig, from polkas in Olean to later varied employers.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Nothing that you decide. If the phone rings you answer it. You know. And you play with whoever — if somebody calls you for a gig and you’ve got to realize growing up in Olean, New York man, I didn’t call myself — we played polkas, we played all kinds of, we played the Sons of Italy and we played all the Italian songs and we’d play pretty much every gig — I could play the “Liechtensteiner Polka,” I could play the “Clarinet Polka,” you know. That’s just how I came up you know. I haven’t played a polka in a long time, but I certainly could if somebody called me to play one.
